{{Quote|In time, things will work out as intended.|Revwien adage|<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />}}
The '''Revwiens''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Plant/Legends|plant]]-like [[Species/Legends|species]]. Their bodies were cylindrical and mounted atop several strong, prehensile leaves, which were used both for locomotion and manipulation of objects. A cluster of tiny budstalks connected a round, clear seedcase to the top of the body. Revwiens came in a variety of [[Color/Legends|colors]], including blue, green, orange, purple, red, and yellow. Their striated leaves ranged from dark green to purplish-black.

The Revwiens were indigenous to [[Revyia]], a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] on the northern edge of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] was covered in jungle and plains, and the Revwiens came to revere the jungle belt as sacred. They developed a philosophy known as the [[Tyia]], which emphasized spiritual unity between individuals. Adherents of the Tyia developed the ability to manipulate [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Revwien society was organized into small autonomous, semi-nomadic groups. Their technological innovation centered around plants, which they used for myriad purposes.

Revyia received only light traffic due to its isolation and attracted little [[Merchant/Legends|trade]]. Following the [[Death/Legends|execution]] of many [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] during [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] at the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], many Revwien Tyia left their homeworld to aid any fugitive Jedi they could track down. The Tyia was one of the few [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] organizations that openly operated during this [[Time/Legends|time]], although most Revwiens avoided conflict with the Empire. From then onward, Revwiens made their way to such diverse locations as [[Fornax Station]], [[Harix]], and [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Revwien [[Wuwuhuul]] joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and participated in a [[Mission to Goratak III|mission]] to the planet [[Goratak III]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Revwien_on_Tatooine.png|thumb|left|250px|A green and yellow Revwien]]
The Revwiens were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Plant/Legends|plant]]-like [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]]. The central trunk of a Revwien body was cylindrical, with a slight bulge at the lower end. The stalk was lightly ribbed and separated into five vertical portions; its [[Color/Legends|color]] was either red, orange, yellow, green, blue, or purple. Stored within the chamber of the central trunk were all the vital organs. Underneath the stalk grew a dense mass of thin, flexible, short [[Limb/Legends|appendages]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

Arrayed at the base of the trunk were between six and eleven leaves. These strong fronds were adapted for seizing, grasping, and manipulating items. They also had an ambulatory function; normally four or more were in use for movement and other support. These leaves could hoist the central trunk off the ground to a height between one-third<ref name="Galaxy Guide" /> to two-thirds of the height of the central stem itself.<ref name="Revised Roleplaying Game" /> This resulted in an average height for Revwiens of between one to two [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide" /> The base leaves came in colors that ranged from red<ref name="Revised Roleplaying Game" /> and dark green to purplish-black and had striations that ran down their length. The leaves terminated in two strands that gave the appearance of fingers.<ref name="Galaxy Guide" /> Some Revwiens also had smaller leaves that sprouted from the top of the central trunk, although these leaves were shorter and remained one strand through to their termination.<ref name="Gamemaster Screen">''[[Star Wars Gamemaster Screen]]''</ref>

An ovoid, clear, seedcase was attached to the top of the trunk by a cluster of tiny budstalks that doubled as visual organs. Further sensory data was obtained through the species' leaves, which sensed fine vibrations and allowed for an analog to hearing. The leaves also provided Revwiens with the senses of touch and smell. The Revwiens gained sustenance from [[Carbon dioxide/Legends|carbon dioxide]] and soil nutrients&mdash;typically dissolved in [[Water/Legends|water]]&mdash;via a [[Chlorophyll/Legends|chlorophyll]] analog. The conversion of these materials into usable forms was powered by [[Star/Legends|sunlight]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

==Society and culture==
===Culture and temperament===
{{Quote|Think of peace and honor&mdash;and act upon that only!|A Revwien Force adept|<ref name="RPG 2nd">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition]]</ref>}}
Revwiens were peaceful beings who valued honor. They were often unfalteringly honest, even when faced with situations in which bending the truth would produce tangible benefits. Revwiens tried to negotiate their way out of conflicts and took an extremely long-term view of issues, as reflected in the popular Revwien idiom that "In time, things will work out as intended." Many Revwiens also exhibited fatalistic tendencies, believing that all things happened for a reason. When no alternative to battle could be found, Revwiens fought with honor, refraining from taking unfair advantage of their enemies.<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

Very little perturbed Revwiens, who showed a remarkable ability to remain calm in stressful situations. However, they did became nervous around overly aggressive or violent individuals, and they found [[Death/Legends|death]] an unsettling concept. Some Revwiens were also ill at ease in the company of other sentient beings who casually cut down plants for use in construction and for materials.<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

[[File:RevwienBMTC.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A Revwien in the midst of a cantina brawl on Harix]]
Only very infrequently did Revwiens wear clothing; however, they did use other accessories for decorative or practical purposes. For instance, some Revwiens wore ribbons and amulets around their central trunk.<ref name="Galaxy Guide" /> A number of Revwiens wore [[Tyia amulet|amulets]] that were representative of the [[Tyia]] philosophy. These talismans had a triangular centerpiece to which were attached green<ref name="RPG 2nd" /> or opalescent beads, as well as green discs.<ref name="Jedi Academy">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> Those Revwiens who lived offworld for long periods took to wearing [[Utility belt/Legends|belts]] for the purposes of carrying weapons, [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]], and other assorted items.<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

===Social organization===
Revwien society was generally organized into small, self-governing communities that lived in groves in the wilds of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Revyia]]. These communities were semi-nomadic, with annual migrations to lakes and rivers. Individuals largely lived in irenic coexistence. This peace was disturbed on occasion by herds of [[Diet/Legends|herbivorous]] creatures that preyed on Revwiens. In order to ward off these threats, some communities domesticated carnivorous animals, such as the large, [[Wolf/Legends|wolf-like]] [[urpine]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

There were two main exceptions to the unorganized Revwien social system. Firstly, Revwien [[University/Legends|universities]] were the sole formal institutions on Revyia. Tuition was conducted in meadows and open woods and produced excellence in learning. Revwiens characteristically spent their lives learning and sharing knowledge with others. Secondly, following the establishment of a small [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Revyia Imperial base|base]] on Revyia, the Revwiens set up a formal [[Spaceport/Legends|starport]] and customs station. Known as [[Revyia Station]], this was the only settlement on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] worthy of being called a [[City/Legends|city]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide" /> An offworld institution linked with the Revwiens was the [[Revwien Comedy Academy Playhouse/Legends|Revwien Comedy Academy Playhouse]], located in the prominent [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]] of the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]], [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="Inside">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref>

===Technology===
{{Quote|Unless you're a plant-based Revwien badly in need of petal-pruning, you have nothing to fear from the docile automated gardeners.|Advertisement for the 5T Tree Feeder|<ref name="Droids">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>}}
Revwien technological innovation centered around cultivating and utilizing plant life. Revwiens made use of plants as adhesives, as well as for healing salves and generating light. Other plants were used to forecast the weather; users interpreted color changes for predictive purposes. Revwiens also utilized plants in place of more conventional weapons. For instance, the [[Vognallian seed pod]]s were thrown in a similar fashion to [[Fragmentation grenade/Legends|fragmentation grenades]]. The seed pods exploded when hurled, and propelled sharp seeds in all directions. Revwiens had a child-like curiosity about offworld technology, and they happily used it alongside their own indigenous innovations, even if they did not understand how the former functioned;<ref name="Galaxy Guide" /> however, problems often arose with automated pruning [[Droid/Legends|droids]], such as the [[R0/5T.N1 tree feeder|5T Tree Feeder]].<ref name="Droids" /> Despite some familiarity with [[Starship/Legends|starships]], Revwiens found it strange to see them in their own skies.<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

===Tyia philosophy===
{{Quote|I am quite certain that the White Current is the Force in the same way that Tyia or Allyan magic are also the Force.|Luke Skywalker, speaking at his [[Jedi Praxeum]]|<ref name="Cracken">''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Revwien_and_Ewok.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Revwien Thuwisten levitates an Ewok.]]
During much of [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|the galaxy's history]], [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] Revwiens withdrew to the jungles to study the Tyia philosophy&mdash;"tyia" was the Revwien word for "breathe."<ref name="Jedi Academy" /> The central tenet of the Tyia philosophy concerned a spiritual unity between individuals. It taught that individuals should seek personal harmony with their "Tyia," which would allow numerous "Tyia" to form a "Thuwisten," namely, a bond-circle formed through the joining of spirits. The Thuwisten would then be complete in utter harmony. Due to this central precept, followers of the Tyia philosophy were called Thuwistens. The Tyia philosophy also emphasized peace and respect for all life.<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

Thuwisten on Revyia spread their beliefs to all who were receptive; however, despite its long history, the religion only became widely known in the galaxy around the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the Galactic Empire. This evangelization was triggered by the killing of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] after the declaration of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]; following these deaths, many Thuwisten were sent into the galaxy to seek out and aid any remaining Jedi. The Tyia was one of a small number of [[The Force/Legends|Force]] traditions that was openly practiced under the Empire; its practitioners largely avoided conflict with Imperial forces.<ref name="Jedi Academy" />

By [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] and leader of the [[New Jedi Order]], was aware of the Tyia philosophy, which he considered to be a manifestation of the Force, analogous to [[Dathomir Magic|Allyan magic]] from [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] or the [[Fallanassi/Legends|Fallanassi]] adepts.<ref name="Cracken" /> Thuwisten manifested many [[Force power/Legends|skills]] similar to those of Jedi, such as [[Force healing/Legends|healing]] skills,<ref name="Jedi Academy" /> [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]], and [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathy]].<ref name="Miniatures">[[Star Wars Miniatures Battles (first edition)|''Star Wars Miniatures Battles'', First Edition]]</ref> Thuwisten typically did not use [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]],<ref name="Jedi Academy" /> although there were some exceptions.<ref name="Miniatures" />

Some Revwien Thuwisten fell to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], which caused them to take on a shriveled appearance. Such individuals were not given names; they lost the right to any such appellation. Any Tyia practitioners who fell to the dark side, whether Revwien or of another species, sought to break out of the cycle of Tyia and inflict this state on as many other individuals as possible.<ref name="Jedi Academy" />

==History==
{{Quote|I went to one of the Meetings out in deepspace, halfway from the Pits of Plooma to the Galactic Rim. All I cared about was sneaking in under the Ithorians' detection screens, handing off about a hundred kilos of rock ivory to Grambo the Worrt and getting out of there before the Imperials caught up with me, and it was still the most&hellip; I dunno.|Han Solo reflects on attending a Herd Meet in space over Revyia|<ref name="Children">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>}}
The Revwiens evolved on Revyia,<ref name="Galaxy Guide" /> a world that was located on the northern fringes of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="TEAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> and which was considered the halfway point between the [[Pits of Plooma/Legends|Pits of Plooma]] and the [[Galactic Rim/Legends|Galactic Rim]].<ref name="Children" /> The planet had a temperate climate, with an equatorial jungle belt and long, rolling plains.<ref name="Jedi Academy" /> The ancient histories of the Revwiens told of a dominant [[Unidentified mythical civilization|civilization]] on the planet, with developed cities and powerful artifacts; however, the authenticity of these legends was disputed by later [[Archaeology/Legends|archaeologists]] who could not unearth any evidence to support such a situation. As Revwien society developed, it formed very few formal institutions; open air universities were an exception. Rather than researching technology, the Revwiens cultivated botanical solutions to meet their needs; plants were used for lighting, adhesives, weather prediction, and even munitions.<ref name="Galaxy Guide" /> The Revwiens eventually became aware of a manifestation of the Force they called the Tyia. Force-sensitive Revwiens spent time in the holy jungle belt to study the Tyia and develop their abilities.<ref name="Jedi Academy" />

[[File:Tyia.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A Jedi consults a Revwien Tyia.]]
Despite its navigational isolation, Revyia became part of the [[Veragi sector/Legends|Veragi sector]],<ref name="TEAOC" /> and the Revwiens received occasional visits from a handful of independently-owned [[Light freighter/Legends|light freighters]]. This traffic produced only light commerce, as the Revwiens had little technology to [[Merchant/Legends|trade]];<ref name="Galaxy Guide" /> however, [[Revwien lettuce]] and [[Revwien coleslaw|coleslaw]] were available as far away as Coruscant, where they were regular ingredients on the menu of [[Dexter Jettster/Legends|Dexter Jettster's]] [[Dex's Diner/Legends|diner]].<ref name="Dex's">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/dexdiner/index.html|text=Dining at Dex's|int=Dining at Dex's}}</ref>

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Tyia masters on Revyia were heavily disturbed by the deaths of so many [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] during the execution of Order 66 by the Galactic Empire at the end of the Clone Wars, which they could sense through the Force. It prompted them to call a meeting within a [[Revyia temple|temple]] grown from the largest [[Tree/Legends|trees]] on their world. They then charged their most capable students with seeking out any remaining Jedi and aiding them in whatever way possible. [[Unidentified Revwien Tyia adept|One such]] Revwien Tyia adept was consulted by a Human Jedi.<ref name="Jedi Academy" />

Sometime between [[14 BBY/Legends|14]] and [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the Revwiens' home [[Star system/Legends|star system]] was the site of an [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorian]] [[Herd Meet/Legends|Time of Meeting]],<ref name="Children" /><ref name="Blog">{{Blog|danwallace|153|Unstated Canon in Star Wars: The Essential Atlas}}</ref> an event in which [[Ithorian Herdship]]s from all across the galaxy gathered to undertake herd business and conduct trade.<ref name="Starfaring Jungles">{{GamerCite|4|Starfaring Jungles}}</ref> The event attracted [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] such as [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Grambo]] the [[Worrt/Legends|Worrt]].<ref name="Children" /> Smugglers also established a [[Revyia smuggler base|base]] deep in the jungles of Revyia. Their presence attracted the attention of the Empire, which [[Skirmish on Revyia|eliminated]] the smugglers and subsequently established a small, permanent presence on Revyia. The Revwiens cooperated with the new Imperial presence and established Revyia Station just outside the Imperial base. They also purchased several run-down [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]]. However, despite these additions, Revyia remained a quiet, undeveloped world.<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

==Revwiens in the galaxy==
[[File:Mission_to_Goratek_III.png|thumb|left|250px|Wuwuhuul and Grindol Maal confront Feskitt Bobb.]]
Most Revwiens in the galaxy were curious wanderers, content to work for passage on starships, as they required little to survive. These travelers generally lacked advanced skills, but they were reliable workers in the tasks they were given. Travel offworld opened new vistas of learning for Revwiens, whose curiosity drove them to learn about even the most routine and simple aspects of galactic life. Revwiens enjoyed having friends; anyone who spoke to them soon became a candidate to follow. While their trust made them ripe to be taken advantage of, their lack of possessions prevented the species from suffering major losses in such encounters.<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

Sometime prior to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="Episode II">{{Film|II}}</ref> a [[Unidentified Revwien merchant/Legends|Revwien trader]] lived in the town of [[Mos Nytram/Legends|Mos Nytram]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. The trader auctioned to local resident [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]] a [[Zephyr-G swoop/Legends|Zephyr-G swoop]] that was later used by Jedi Knight [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] to track down and slaughter the [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] who had captured his [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|mother]].<ref name="Incredible">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref><ref name="Owen Lars">{{DB|vehicle|owenbike|swoop bike, Owen Lars'}}</ref>

The Revwien [[Wuwuhuul]] lived during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. As a Thuwisten, Wuwuhuul was competent in several Force powers and wielded a lightsaber.<ref name="Miniatures" /> Wuwuhuul traveled with the ex-[[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] sympathizer [[Grindol Maal]]. When Maal volunteered to lead a group of Rebel [[operative]]s in a [[Mission to Goratak III|mission]] to capture an [[I2-CG droid/Legends|I2-CG]] droid that contained vital intelligence that had crashed on [[Goratak III]], Wuwuhuul accompanied the ex-pirate. Together with the [[Red Smoke]], [[Safari One]], and [[Buzz Boys]] [[Squad/Legends|squads]], Wuwuhuul and Maal clashed with Imperial forces under the command of [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Feskitt Bobb]].<ref name="Miniatures" />

Sometime between [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]] and 0 BBY, a [[Unidentified Revwien (Fornax Station)|Revwien]] was present on [[Fornax Station]] and observed the [[Fire Rings of Fornax|Five Fire Rings of Fornax]], a spectacular natural phenomenon.<ref name="Fornax">''[[Adventures in Hyperspace: Fire Ring Race]]''</ref> In 0 BBY, a green- and yellow-colored [[Unidentified Revwien (Tatooine)|Revwien]] was outside [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] on Tatooine when the exiled Jedi Master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] took Luke Skywalker there to search for a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] to take them offworld.<ref name="Droids 6">[[Droids (1986) 6|''Droids'' (1986) 6]]</ref> Later, in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], a [[Unidentified Revwien (space-freighter)|purple Revwien]] was present at a [[Unidentified space-freighter's hangout|space-freighter's hangout]]. A brawl underway in the hangout was interrupted when local schoolboy [[Berd Lin]] burst in and recruited many of the patrons in an effort to rescue his [[Myoris Lin|mother]] from Imperial forces who had arrested her.<ref name="Classic">{{StoryCite|story=Bring Me the Children|book=Classic Star Wars: The Early Adventures 7}}</ref> Another [[Unidentified Revwien Thuwisten|Revwien Thuwisten]] once encountered and levitated an [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]], a species native to the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].<ref name="Gamemaster Screen" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Revwien-MAAFGL.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Ron Cobb's Revwien design]]
The Revwien species was designed by [[Ron Cobb]] as one of a series of sketches for denizens of the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] scene in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="Art">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope]]''</ref> Cobb's designs were intended for additional U.S. shooting of the cantina scene;<ref name="Chronicles">[[Star Wars Chronicles|''Star Wars: Chronicles'']]</ref> however, ultimately, the Revwien sketch proved too complex to turn into a costume,<ref name="Topps 1">{{Topps|set=1993 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 1|cardname=#18: Hammerhead|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/75144/cid/5338678/1993-Topps-Star-Wars-Galaxy-18-Hammerhead}}</ref> so the species was not included in the film.<ref name="A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref> Cobb's concept art was then published in several reference books, firstly in ''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope]]'' in [[1979]], and later in the [[Star Wars Technical Journal of the Planet Tatooine|''Star Wars Technical Journal'']] ([[1993]]) and [[Star Wars Chronicles|''Star Wars: Chronicles'']] ([[1997]]). These sources included Cobb's design notes for the species, which read, "Tropical Rain Forest / (Ambulatory Plant) / Traps and absorbs insect-like creatures. Great sense of humor&mdash;best joke-tellers in the galaxy."<ref name="Chronicles" /> The ''Technical Journal'' suggests the concept art was actually a sketch by an artist who saw the alien while visiting the cantina.<ref name="Tech Journal">''[[Star Wars Technical Journal of the Planet Tatooine]]''</ref> Another species named [[Parwan/Legends|Parwan]] was later created based on the same piece of concept art.<ref name="SW-The Box - The Clone Wars Episode Guide">{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep417|text="The Box" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}}</ref>

The first [[canon]]ical appearance of the Revwien species occurred in [[1987]] with the publication of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] [[Droids (1986) 6|''Droids'' (1986) 6]], although the species was not named in the comic. The name "Revwien" was first applied to the species in [[1991]] with the inclusion of a member of the species in [[Star Wars Miniatures Battles (first edition)|''Star Wars Miniatures Battles'']], published by [[West End Games]]. The book presented the Revwien as an "Alien Student of the Force,"<ref name="Miniatures" /> a role that was later reprised in a number of other West End Games products.<ref name="RPG 2nd" /><ref name="Revised Roleplaying Game" /> West End Games also created a miniature Revwien, which it included in its "Rebel Characters" and "Aliens of the Galaxy 1" [[Star Wars Miniatures Battles#Blister Packs|miniature sets]].<ref name="Miniatures" />

In [[1995]], a Revwien appeared in the background of [[Classic Star Wars: The Early Adventures 7|''Classic Star Wars: The Early Adventures'' 7]], which republished ''[[Bring Me the Children]]'', originally a newspaper comic strip by [[Russ Manning]] that had been published by the [[Los Angeles Times Syndicate]] in [[1980]]. The Revwien in the scene was not actually present in the original newspaper strip but was added to the panel to make it better fit a comic book rather than newspaper format.<ref name="Classic" /> Later in 1995, the culture and history of the Revwien species was significantly expanded with the release of [[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies|''Galaxy Guide 12 Aliens — Enemies and Allies'']]. Their entry was written by [[Harry Heckel]], and they were illustrated by [[Mike Vilardi]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide" />

The cover of [[Star Wars Manga: A New Hope 2|''Star Wars Manga: A New Hope'' 2]] ([[1998]]) depicted a Revwien in the Mos Eisley cantina, a scene that reflected the origins of Cobb's sketch; however, the image was not replicated inside the actual comic. Following references in ''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]'' ([[1999]]), ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections]]'' ([[2002]]), and the non-canon comic book "[[The Emperor's Court]]" (2002), [[Dorling Kindersley]]'s ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]'' ([[2003]]) introduced the Revwien Comedy Academy Playhouse.<ref name="Inside" /> This appears to be a reference to Cobb's original design notes, which described the species as the best joke-tellers in the galaxy.<ref name="Chronicles" />

[[Wizards of the Coast]] included the Revwiens in its [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game|roleplaying game]], with an extensive entry in the ''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]'' ([[2009]]), and an illustration by [[Adam Gillespie]]. However, its coverage of the Revwiens differed with previously established West End Games material by stating that, "For much of the galaxy's history, Revwien Force-users studied the Tyia and developed a kind of religion out it, spreading the word of their beliefs to any who would believe it." The earlier West End Games material had stated that, "Nearly 30 years ago, one of the independent freighters brought to Revyia a missionary who belonged to the faith known simply as Tyia." Where the accounts are in conflict, this article has favored that of Wizards of the Coast, as it is the most recently published source material.

In ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' (2009), authors [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]] placed the Revwien homeworld and [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] a passage from the novel [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']] (1995) to refer to Revyia.<ref name="Children" /><ref name="Blog" /> Revyia was placed very close to&mdash;and possibly within&mdash;the borders of the [[Gree Enclave/Legends|Gree Enclave]], which is home to the [[Gree (species)/Legends|Gree]], an ancient species that predated the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and which was renowned for its unique and powerful [[Gree technology|technology]].<ref name="Gree">{{JournalCite|8|The Gree Enclave}}</ref> When asked if the Gree Enclave was intended to be the source of the Revwien myths of a dominant civilization on their homeworld, Fry responded that the placement was probably luck, but that a "Gree/Revyia connection sounds very plausible, though."<ref name="Fry Gree">{{JCFCite|url=posts/30941648|board=Literature|thread=The Essential Atlas and Galactic Cartography: Official Discussion|user=[[Jason Fry|jasonfry]]|date=2010-05-19|time=1:47 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802112633/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-essential-atlas-and-galactic-cartography-official-discussion.21938930/page-144}}</ref>

===Non-canon content===
[[File:Revwien_Tales.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Revwien in ''The Emperor's Court'']]
{{Quote|Where have you been?<br />Why haven't you called?|[[Unidentified introspective Revwien|An introspective Revwien]]|<ref name="George">''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]''</ref>}}
A cleaned-up version of Cobb's original sketch is included in ''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]'' (1993), a non-canon publication that combines creature designs and photographs from various [[George Lucas]] projects with original text by [[Bob Carrau]]. This book accompanies the Cobb image with a small monologue presented as if the Revwien is drowning its sorrows while having drink after breaking up with its partner.<ref name="George" />

A Revwien also appeared in the background of ''The Emperor's Court'', published in [[Star Wars Tales 14|''Star Wars Tales'' 14]], an [[Infinities]] comic story. In ''The Emperor's Court'', Han Solo is on trial for killing the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]], with different versions of evidence presented based on competing versions of the Mos Eisley cantina scene as depicted in the original and [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|''Special Edition'']] releases of ''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope''. This comic appears to be a parody of the television show [[Wikipedia:The People's Court|''The People's Court'']].<ref name="Emperor's Court">{{Tales|14|The Emperor's Court}}</ref>
